Subject:  Intimation of 3 3rd Annual General Meeting (“AGM”) of the Company  & 
submission of Integrated Annual Report for the Financial Year 202 4-25  
  
Dear Sir / Madam , 
 
Pursuant to the Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we hereby inform that 3 3rd AGM of the Company will 
be held on Thursday, September 2 5, 202 5 at 01:00 P .M. (IST)  through Video 
Conferencing  (‘VC’) /Other Audi o Visual Means  (‘OAVM’) . 
 
Further, pursuant to the Regulation 44 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the Company will be providing the facility for voting 
by electronic means (“remote e -voting”). The remote e -voting period will commence on 
Sunday, September 2 1, 202 5 (9:00 a.m. IST) and end on Wednesday, September 2 4, 
2025 (5:00 p.m. IST). The voting rights of Members shall be reckoned on the basis of 
number of equity shares held by Members of the Company as on the cut -off date viz. 
Thursday , September 1 8, 2025.  
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30, 34(1) , 36 & other relevant regulations as applicable  of SEBI 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we are enclosing 
herewith Integrated  Annual  Report of the Company for Financial Year 202 4-25 along 
with the notice of 3 3rd AGM of the Company .  
 
The aforesaid documents are also hosted on the website of the Company viz. 
www.lemontreehotels.com   
 
Please take the above intimation on your record.  
 
Thanking you,  
 
For Lemon Tree Hotels Limited

 How do I vote electronically using NSDL e-Voting system?
 The way to vote electronically on NSDL e-Voting system consists of “Two Steps” which are mentioned below:
 Step 1: Access to NSDL e-Voting system
A)  Login method for e-Voting and joining virtual meeting for Individual shareholders holding securities 
in demat mode
  In terms of SEBI circular dated December 9, 2020 on e-Voting facility provided by Listed Companies, 
Individual shareholders holding securities in demat mode are allowed to vote through their demat account 
maintained with Depositories and Depository Participants. Shareholders are advised to update their mobile 
number and email Id in their demat accounts to access e-Voting facility.
 Login method for Individual shareholders holding securities in demat mode is given below:
Type of shareholders  Login Method
Individual Shareholders 
holding securities in 
demat mode with NSDL.1.  For OTP based login you can click on https://eservices.nsdl.com/SecureWeb/evoting/
evotinglogin.jsp . You will have to enter your 8-digit DP ID,8-digit Client Id, PAN No., 
Verification code and generate OTP. Enter the OTP received on registered email id/mobile 
number and click on login. After successful authentication, you will be redirected to NSDL 
Depository site wherein you can see e-Voting page. Click on company name or e-Voting 
service provider i.e. NSDL and you will be redirected to e-Voting website of NSDL for 
casting your vote during the remote e-Voting period or joining virtual meeting & voting 
during the meeting.
2.  Existing IDeAS user can visit the e-Services website of NSDL Viz. https://eservices.
nsdl.com either on a Personal Computer or on a mobile. On the e-Services home page 
click on the “Beneficial Owner” icon under “Login” which is available under ‘IDeAS’ 
section, this will prompt you to enter your existing User ID and Password. After successful 
authentication, you will be able to see e-Voting services under Value added services. Click 
on “Access to e-Voting” under e-Voting services and you will be able to see e-Voting 
page. Click on company name or e-Voting service provider i.e. NSDL and you will be 
re-directed to e-Voting website of NSDL for casting your vote during the remote e-Voting 
period or joining virtual meeting & voting during the meeting.
3.  If you are not registered for IDeAS e-Services, option to register is available at https://
eservices.nsdl.com . Select “Register Online for IDeAS Portal”  or click at https://
eservices.nsdl.com/SecureWeb/IdeasDirectReg.jsp
4.  Visit the e-Voting website of NSDL. Open web browser by typing the following URL: 
https://www.evoting.nsdl.com/ either on a Personal Computer or on a mobile. Once the 
home page of e-Voting system is launched, click on the icon “Login” which is available 
under ‘Shareholder/Member’ section. A new screen will open. You will have to enter your 
User ID (i.e. your sixteen-digit demat account number hold with NSDL), Password/OTP 
and a Verification Code as shown on the screen. After successful authentication, you 
will be redirected to NSDL Depository site wherein you can see e-Voting page. Click on 
company name or e-Voting service provider i.e. NSDL and you will be redirected to 
e-Voting website of NSDL for casting your vote during the remote e-Voting period or 
joining virtual meeting & voting during the meeting.
5.  Shareholders/Members can also download NSDL Mobile App “NSDL Speede”  facility by 
scanning the QR code mentioned below for seamless voting experience.

Item No. 3 
Appointment of M/s DPV & Associates 
LLP, Practicing Company Secretaries, as 
Secretarial Auditors of the Company
Pursuant to SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2024 
(“Listing Regulations”), effective from 1st April, 2025, 
a Company is required to appoint peer reviewed 
secretarial auditor (if individual then for not more 
than one term of five consecutive years and if a firm 
then for not more than two terms of five consecutive 
years), with the approval of the shareholders in the 
Annual General Meeting.
Accordingly, the Board of Directors of the Company 
at their meeting held on May 29, 2025, on the 
recommendation of the Audit Committee and after 
considering the experience, market standing, 
efficiency of the audit teams and independence, 
have appointed M/s DPV & Associates LLP, Practicing 
Company Secretaries (Firm Registration Number: 
L2021HR009500) as the Secretarial Auditors of the 
Company for a term of 5 (five) consecutive financial 
years commencing from April 01, 2025 till March 31, 
2030, subject to the approval of the Members of the 
Company in ensuing Annual General Meeting.
M/s DPV & Associates LLP is a peer reviewed and 
a well-established firm of Practicing Company 
Secretaries, registered with the Institute of Company 
Secretaries of India (ICSI).
M/s DPV & Associates LLP is devoted towards 
providing a wide gamut of high-quality advisory 
services and solutions to a wide network of clients 
all over India in the field of Corporate Laws, IPO 
advisory, Due Diligence, Legal Drafting, Opinions, 
Corporate Restructuring, Merger/Amalgamations, 
Related Party Transactions, FEMA, SEBI Compliances, 
especially in the core area of Company Law matters. 
The firm is led by experienced partners, all of whom 
are professionals in the field of corporate governance 
and compliance.
M/s DPV & Associates LLP has given their consent to 
act as Secretarial Auditors and provided confirmation 
that they hold a valid peer review certificate issued by 
ICSI and that they are not disqualified to be appointed 
as the Secretarial Auditors of the Company in the 
terms of the provisions of the Listing Regulations, the 
Companies Act, 2013 and the Rules made thereunder.
Subject to the approval of the shareholders in the 
33rd Annual General Meeting, the Board of Directors in consultation with the Audit Committee may alter 
and vary the terms and conditions of appointment, 
including remuneration, in such manner and to 
such extent as may be mutually agreed with the 
Secretarial Auditors.
The Board recommends the resolution set out at Item 
No. 3 of the Notice for approval by the shareholders by 
way of an Ordinary Resolution. None of the Directors 
or Key Managerial Personnel of the Company or their 
relatives are interested or concerned, financially or 
otherwise, in the resolution.

Approval of one-time Ex-gratia payment 
to Mr. Patanjali Govind Keswani 
(DIN:00002974), Chairman & Managing 
Director of the Company
During the COVID-19 situation the hospitality and 
leisure industry was among the first to experience 
severe and adverse conditions. The industry remained 
focused on assessing and quantifying the operational 
and financial impact on business performance. 
This impact was significant and, to a large extent, 
remained unpredictable, particularly with respect to 
revenue and supply chains. During this period, the 
management took proactive measures to mitigate 
challenges related to cash flows and working capital.
During the challenging COVID-19 period, i.e. 
FY 2020-21 and 2021-22, the employees of the 
Company voluntarily waived off all or part of their 
remuneration to support the Company’s financial 
position, with no non-voluntary pay-cuts imposed 
during this time. This also included Mr. Patanjali 
Govind Keswani, Managing Director of the Company, 
who voluntarily waived up to 100% of his approved 
remuneration in financial years 2020-21 and 2021-22 
in order to support the Company’s financial position.
The Company after returning to profitability post 
covid period, decided to pay one time ex-gratia to 
continuing employees towards the salary voluntarily 
waived by them during the COVID-19 period.
In recognition of this gesture and contribution during 
an unprecedented period, it is proposed to pay 
Mr. Patanjali Govind Keswani, Managing Director of 
the Company, one time ex-gratia of H 460.76 Lakhs, 
equivalent to the salary voluntarily waived by him, 
which will be due and payable in March, 2026, in 
addition to his proposed remuneration as Executive 
Director and Chairman as set out at Item No. 5 of 
this 33rd AGM Notice. The Company will ensure that 
all other continuing employees who had similarly 
volunteered to waive a part of their remuneration 
are paid their commensurate one-time ex-gratia 
amounts prior to payment of the above ex-gratia to 
Mr. Patanjali Govind Keswani.
The Board of Directors recommend the resolution as 
set out at Item No. 11 of this 33rd AGM Notice relating 
to the payment of one time Ex-gratia of H 460.76 Lakhs 
to Mr. Patanjali Govind Keswani, Managing Director 
of the Company for approval of the shareholders 
as Special Resolution. The payment of Ex-gratia as 
approved by the Board and the shareholders shall be 
paid to him in the event of the inadequacy of profits, 
which may exceed the amount calculated under 
Schedule V of the Act.
Mr. Patanjali Govind Keswani, Mr. Aditya Madhav

resolution at Item No. 11. None of the other Directors,

Mr. Niten Malhan is the founder and managing 
partner of New Mark Advisors LLP, an investment 
manager focused on applying the principles of 
private equity investing to small and mid-sized listed 
Indian companies with an aim to achieve long term 
compounding of capital. Prior to founding New Mark 
Advisors LLP in April 2018, he was the managing 
director and co-head of India at Warburg Pincus 
India Private Limited (“Warburg Pincus”), a global 
private equity firm. Mr. Niten Malhan joined Warburg 
Pincus in 2001 and became a partner at the firm in 
2007. In 2012, he was appointed the co-head of the 
India business, co-leading a team of 15 investment 
professionals and a portfolio of over $3 billion in value. 
Between 2012 and 2017, Niten was also a member of 
the global executive management group of the firm, 
a group of senior partners who lead different offices 
and industry groups at Warburg Pincus.
Prior to joining Warburg Pincus, he worked as 
director of business development at Stratum 8, a 
Silicon Valley technology start-up company. Before 
that, he was an engagement manager at McKinsey & 
Company, and worked in the India, South East Asia 
and Boston offices of the firm.
Mr. Niten studied Computer Science & Engineering 
at Indian Institute of Technology, New Delhi, and 
completed his Post Graduate Diploma in Management 
from Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad. 
Niten is a Founder and Trustee of Plaksha University

Details of the employees who are

All Eligible employees as per the Scheme to whom

SAR units have been granted to the employees, hence

the interests of the employees who are beneficiaries 
under the scheme.
In terms of Section 62(1)(b) of the Companies Act, 
2013 read with Regulation 6 & 7 of the Securities 
and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee 
Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 [“SEBI 
(SBEB & SE) Regulations, 2021”] the Company seeks 
your approval for implementation of the Scheme and 
grant SAR Units thereunder to the eligible employees 
as per the Scheme.
Features of the proposed Scheme are specified under:
a) Brief description of the Scheme:
  The Scheme seeks to reward Eligible employees 
by way of granting stock appreciation rights, with 
a view to reward their association and loyalty 
which has resulted in corporate growth and value 
creation over a long period of time.
  This Scheme shall be called the “LTHL -Stock 
Appreciation Rights Scheme – 2024” 
hereinafter referred as “the Scheme”.
 Implementation of the Scheme:-
The Company proposes to implement the 
Scheme through Direct Route for extending 
benefits to Employees wherein the Company will 
distribute in the form of Shares in accordance 
with the Scheme. The Scheme shall continue to 
be in effect up to 8 years from the effective date 
of the scheme unless terminated earlier by the 
Board of Directors.
 Eligibility Criteria’s:-
The Committee may on the basis of all or any of 
the following criteria, decide on the Employees / 
Grantees who are eligible for the grant / vesting 
of SAR Units under the Scheme and the terms 
and conditions thereof.
 •  Loyalty: To be determined on the basis 
of tenure of employment of an Employee 
/ Grantee in the Company and its 
existing Subsidiary.
 •  Performance of Employee / Grantee: 
Performance during the financial year on 
the basis of the parameters decided by the 
Board of Directors or Committee. •  Performance of Company: Performance of 
the Company as per the standards set by 
the Board of Directors or Committee.
Any other criteria as decided by the Committee 
in consultation with Board of Directors from time 
to time.
b) Total number of SARs to be granted:
The maximum number of SAR Units that may be 
issued pursuant to this Scheme shall not exceed 
1,50,00,000 and the maximum number of Shares 
that may be issued and allotted pursuant to 
exercise of SAR Units shall not exceed 80,00,000 
at a face value of H 10 each.
If any SAR Unit granted under the Scheme 
lapses or is forfeited or surrendered under any 
provision of the Scheme, such SAR Unit shall be 
added back to the pool and shall be available for 
further grant under the Scheme unless otherwise 
determined by the Committee.
Further, the maximum number of SAR Units that 
can be granted and the Shares arise upon exercise 
of these SAR Units shall stand adjusted in case of 
corporate action, as defined in the Scheme.
c)  Identification of classes of employees entitled 
to participate and be Beneficiaries in the 
Scheme:
 Employee means
 (i)  an employee as designated by the company, 
who is exclusively working in India or outside 
India; or
 (ii)  a director of the company, whether a whole-
time director or not, including a nonexecutive 
director who is not a promoter or member 
of the promoter group, but excluding an 
independent director; or
 (iii)  an employee as defined in sub-clauses (i) 
or (ii), of the existing unlisted subsidiaries 
Company, in India or outside India of the 
Company, but does not include—
  (a)  an employee who is a promoter or 
a person belonging to the promoter 
group; or
  (b)  a director who, either himself or 
through his relative or through anybody 
corporate, directly or indirectly, holds 
more than ten per cent of the outstanding 
equity shares of the company;
  “Eligible Employee” means those employees 
who have been identified as Eligible on meeting 
the eligibility criteria set by the Nomination and 
Remuneration Committee.

Upon vesting of SAR Units, the Committee in

and terms of grant, shall calculate the 
Appreciation occurred on such SAR Units. The 
Appreciation value in this case will be based 
on the difference between the market price on 
Respective Vesting Date and SAR Price.
“Vesting Date Price” means the price which is 
calculated by the Committee at the time of vesting 
of SAR Units with the Grantees. The Vesting Date 
Price shall be calculated based upon the market 
price on respective vesting Date.For the purpose of the Scheme, SAR Price shall 
be calculated on the basis of Market price as 
defined in the Scheme.
For the purpose of above:
“Market price” means the latest available closing 
price on a recognised stock exchange on which 
the Shares of the Company are listed on the date 
immediately prior to the relevant date.
“Relevant date” means, -
 i)  In the case of grant, the date of the meeting 
of the Committee on which the grant is 
made; or
 ii)  In the case of vesting, the date of vesting of 
SAR Units ; or
 iii)  In the case of exercise, the date on which 
the notice/letter of exercise is given to the 
Company by the Grantee.
g)  Exercise period/offer period, and process of 
exercise/ acceptance of Shares:
The vested SAR Units can be exercised by 
Grantees within the exercise period which shall 
be 1 (one) year from the vesting date.
The vested SAR Units shall be exercisable either 
wholly or in part, according to the terms and 
conditions as determined and mentioned under 
the vesting letter. However, in case of fraction of 
a vested SAR Unit, no Unit shall be exercisable.
Upon exercising, the Grantee shall be entitled 
to receive such number of Equity Shares in lieu 
of appreciation earned. The number of Equity 
Shares to be rewarded shall be determined by 
the Committee, by dividing the Appreciation 
amount by Exercise Date Price.
In the event of doubt in respect of determination 
of relevant date and market price, the Committee 
shall have the discretion, in compliance with SEBI 
(SBEB & SE) Regulations and terms of grant, to 
calculate Exercise Date Price, based on the facts 
relating to each exercise.

Act, 2013 (“the Act”) and SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 
with key emphasis on effective governance, risk 
management, statutory compliances etc. and thereby 
placing increased accountability on the Board.
The role and responsibilities of the Board particularly 
the Non-executive Directors have increased more 
requiring greater time commitments and attention, 
which reflects in the financial performance. The 
Board is of the view that it is necessary that adequate 
compensation be given to the Non-Executive Directors

resolution authorising the Board of Directors for

prescribed in Section 198 of the Companies Act, 2013 
in any financial year in pursuance of Section 197 of 
the Companies Act, 2013 commencing from April 01, 
2025 upto March 31, 2030.

under Item No. 16 for the approval of members as 
Ordinary Resolution.

I. General Information:
1.  Nature of Industry: 
The Company is engaged in the hotel business 
since 2004. Lemon Tree Hotels Limited (LTHL) 
is one of the largest hotel chains in India, and 
owns/ leases/ operates/ franchises hotels across 
the upscale, upper-midscale, midscale and 
economy segments. LTHL delivers differentiated 
yet superior service offerings, with a compelling 
value proposition. The group offers seven brands 
to meet guests’ needs across all levels, viz. 
Aurika Hotels & Resorts, Lemon Tree Premier, 
Lemon Tree Hotels, Red Fox Hotels by Lemon 
Tree Hotels, Keys Prima by Lemon Tree Hotels, 
Keys Select by Lemon Tree Hotels and Keys Lite 
by Lemon Tree Hotels.LTHL opened its first hotel with 49 rooms in May 
2004. Today, the company has a portfolio of 220+ 
hotels, which includes over 110 operational hotels 
and more than 110 hotels set to open in India and 
internationally. Lemon Tree Hotels are located 
across metro regions, including the NCR, Mumbai, 
Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai, as 
well as numerous tier I, II and III cities such as 
Pune, Ahmedabad, Chandigarh, Jaipur, Indore, 
Aurangabad, Udaipur, Visakhapatnam, Kochi, 
Ludhiana, Thiruvananthapuram, Vijayawada 
etc. The company expanded internationally 
with hotels opening in Dubai in December 2019, 
in Bhutan in February 2020 and in Nepal in 
April 2024.
2.  Date or expected date of commencement of 
commercial production:
As of March 31, 2025, the Lemon Tree Hotels 
Group, operates 111 hotels with 10,269 rooms 
across 70+ destinations in India and overseas. 
The group also maintains a robust growth pipeline 
(mainly under management) with 101 hotels 
and 6,847 rooms under development, offering 
a strong foundation of operational depth, brand 
equity, and scalability.Annexure-B

III. Other information:
1. Reasons of loss or inadequate profits:
The Company has delivered an excellent performance during the Financial Year 2024-25, recording a strong profit of H 10,048.74 Lakhs for the year. 
While the Company is confident of sustaining profitability going forward, however the limits prescribed under Section 197(1) read with Schedule V of 
the Companies Act, 2013 and applicable Listing Regulations for the purpose of payment of managerial remuneration, may be considered inadequate, 
primarily on account of payment of one-time Ex-gratia towards the remuneration voluntarily foregone by Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer 
during the unprecedented COVID-19 period, as a gesture of commitment at that time.
Further, in compliance with our succession policy and to further strengthen leadership, the Company has inducted new members on the Board, by 
appointing Managing Director and Executive Director to drive the next phase of growth, subject to Members’ approval.
In view of the aforesaid explanation, approval is sought from Members for payment of managerial remuneration in the event of loss or inadequacy of 
profits during any financial year.
2.  Steps taken or proposed to be taken for improvement and expected increase in productivity and profits in measurable terms:
The management is pursuing various strategic and operational measures that is expected to result in the improvement of profitability of the Company. 
The management is continuous focus on the growth with extension of the network of hotels. The management believes all these strategic initiatives will 
result in better and improved profits for the Company.

Drawing inspiration from India’s rich cultural 
heritage and its dynamic economic growth, 
Lemon Tree Hotels is committed to offering 
accessible, high-quality hospitality across 
tier I, II and III cities. We are aligned with 
the aspirations of India’s rising middle 
class, providing affordable accommodation 
that meets the evolving needs of modern 
travellers. Our expansion is rooted in the 
country’s diverse culture, empowering local 
communities while delivering meaningful 
travel experiences. 
At the same time, we remain dedicated 
to responsible growth. By adopting an 
asset-light model and embracing sustainable 
practices, we ensure that our growth is both 
scalable and environmentally conscious. 
Our commitment to Environmental, Social 
and Governance (ESG) initiatives, such as 
reducing water consumption and increasing 
the use of renewable energy, demonstrates 
our effort to contribute positively to India’s 
future. We also prioritise inclusivity by 
creating employment opportunities for 
marginalised communities. As we continue 
to grow, our focus remains on responsible 
expansion that supports India’s long-term 
socio-economic development, benefiting all 
sections of society.
Inspired by India, 
Growing Responsibly Running Ahead  
of the Curve
Lemon Tree Hotels Limited is India’s largest 
mid-market hotel chain with over 110 hotels and 
10,000+ rooms across 73 destinations, including 
metros, tier-II and emerging cities. Founded 
in 2002, it has grown through a mix of owned, 
leased, managed and franchised properties, 
becoming a leader in India’s hospitality sector.
 
With a multi-brand portfolio spanning economy 
to upscale segments, Lemon Tree caters to both 
business and leisure travellers. Its asset-light 
expansion, digital capabilities and sustainability 
focus drive scalable and profitable growth. As of 
FY25, the Company has achieved 85% of its CY28 
goal of 20,000 rooms (operational and under-
development), showing fast -paced growth.
 
Guided by its vision to be India’s preferred 
mid-market hotel brand, Lemon Tree remains 
committed to operational excellence, guest 
satisfaction and responsible growth. Tigerland Safari - A Lemon Tree Resort, Chitwan, Nepal

Lemon Tree Hotels shall be the 
largest and most preferred Indian 
chain of upscale, upper -midscale, 
midscale and economy hotels 
and resorts.Mission
We shall be committed to:
• Ensuring the well-being and self-worth of our colleagues, who are of 
the utmost importance to us.
• Contributing to the community we live in and to India in general.

A Growing Opportunity
The Indian tourism sector continues on a growth 
trajectory. In 2024, the sector contributed 
approximately  I21 trillion ($244.53 billion) to India’s 
GDP, accounting for 6.6% of the economy6/7. 
With a strong surge in domestic tourism and an 
increasing number of international visitors, India 
continues to solidify its position as a global tourism 
hub8. Government initiatives are transforming the 
sector, thereby offering expansion opportunities to 
hotel companies.
As India strengthens its position of being one of 
the fastest-growing tourism markets globally, 
Lemon Tree Hotels is well placed to emerge 
as a homegrown champion with international 
benchmarks. Our mid-market positioning resonates 
with the aspirations of India’s rising middle class 
while also attracting global travellers seeking 
value-driven yet high-quality experiences. 
With India poised to become one of the world’s 
top travel destinations, we see ourselves not just 
as participants but as contributors to shaping the 
global hospitality narrative.
Connectivity and Consumption 
Tailwinds
The demand for travel in India is being further 
fuelled by unprecedented improvements 
in infrastructure and rising consumption. 
The Government’s emphasis on new airports, 
expressways and the rollout of high-speed Vande 
Bharat trains is reshaping connectivity across 
the country, opening up new destinations and 
making travel more seamless. At the same time, 
the aspirations of India’s growing middle class, 
coupled with rising disposable incomes, are 
driving demand for leisure, wellness and spiritual 
tourism. These trends provide Lemon Tree 
Hotels with a unique opportunity to deepen its 
presence in both established urban centres and 
emerging destinations.CHAIRMAN AND MANAGING DIRECTOR’S MESSAGE

It gives me great pleasure to present the fourth Integrated 
Annual Report (and fifth ESG disclosure) of Lemon Tree Hotels 
for FY25. This year has been marked by significant growth and 
transformation. As we continue to build a substantial inventory 
base, our focus remains on driving sustainable growth alongside 
operational excellence. Our performance this year reflects the 
effectiveness of our strategy and our commitment to providing 
exceptional value to all stakeholders.
In FY25, Lemon Tree Hotels reinforced its status as a leading 
mid-market hospitality brand in India, consistently ranking 
among the top five in terms of media visibility. Our share 
of voice ranged between 3% and 9%5 during the year, 
peaking with announcements of strategic expansions and

In FY25, we delivered a record revenue of 
I1,288.4 Crores, reflecting a 20% YoY growth driven 
by higher room revenue and a strong increase in 
occupancy and Average Daily Rates (ADR). Our Net 
EBITDA stood at I636.46 Crores, marking a 20% 
YoY increase, while Profit After Tax (PAT) reached 
I243.15 Crores, representing a 34% growth. 
Operational efficiency across our hotels played a 
key role in these strong results.
Room occupancy reached 71.7%9, supported by 
a higher ADR across all our brands, bolstered by 
product upgrades, renovations and enhanced guest 
services. We continued our asset-light growth 
strategy, adding 3,784 new rooms through 61 
new openings and signings, bringing our total to 
17,116 rooms across 212 hotels in 131 destinations. 
We are on track to meet our target of 20,000 rooms 
by CY28.
Strategic Goals and Roadmap – 
Lemon Tree 2.0
Lemon Tree Hotels, India’s largest and most trusted 
mid-market hotel chain, is committed to expanding 
its leadership position through the Lemon Tree 2.0 
strategy. Having achieved 85% of its CY28 inventory 
target nearly three years ahead of schedule, our 
Company is focused on delivering superior financial 
performance, accelerating asset-light growth and 
leveraging digital transformation to enhance guest 
experiences and improve operational efficiency.In May 2024, Lemon Tree Hotels 
celebrated 20 years since opening 
the first property in Udyog Vihar, 
Gurugram, marking the first 
milestone in our growth journey.

12  Reduction in intensity terms vs. the FY19 baselineAt the heart of our strategy is asset-light 
growth, with expansion through managed and 
franchised hotels to maximise scalability with 
minimal capital investment. We aim to reach 
a 20,000 -room network by CY28, with more 
than 70% of our portfolio being asset-light. This 
will be complemented by retail acceleration to 
increase direct bookings and reduce reliance on 
third-party platforms, while expanding our Infinity

We are also driving digital transformation to 
leverage Bionic Revenue Management, automate 
processes and make data-driven decisions in order 
to improve profitability. To ensure flexibility in our 
growth while maintaining a strong balance sheet, we 
will continue to optimise our cost structure and be 
best-in-class.
Another key component of our strategy is 
sustainability. Lemon Tree Hotels is committed to 
achieving 100% green-certified hotels (owned/
leased) by FY26, aligned with global standards 
for responsible growth. This includes eco-friendly 
designs, energy-efficient solutions and water 
recycling and reuse across our properties.
Lemon Tree’s strategy has led to operational gains 
and increased visibility in industry platforms and 
in media. This has been reflected in a sustained 
growth in brand mentions in top publications like 
The Economic Times and IndianRetailer.com10.
For us, sustainability is not an adjunct but 
a cornerstone of Lemon Tree 2.0. We firmly 
believe that our growth must be in harmony with 
the environment and society. From pioneering 
energy -efficient hotels to creating one of the most 
inclusive workforces in the industry, we view ESG 
not as a compliance requirement but as a driver of 
innovation, efficiency and long-term value.
ESG Vision and Highlights
Lemon Tree Hotels is dedicated to becoming a 
leader in ESG with clear targets for sustainability 
and diversity. By FY26, our goal is to achieve 30% 
women on our board, while in the workforce we aim 
for 15% women and 20% Opportunity-Deprived 
Individuals (ODIs). Our environmental targets for 
FY26 include reducing energy intensity by 15%, water intensity by 10% and GHG intensity by 40% 
vs. the FY19 baseline. Renewable energy is targeted 
at 50% and we aim to achieve 100% green-certified 
buildings (owned/leased properties) by FY26.
In FY25, we made significant progress, certifying 
34.15%11 of our hotels as green buildings 
and reducing water intensity by 13.73%12. 
Our renewable energy exit rate stood at 27.93% in 
March 2025, with FY26 set for a significant jump 
to 50%. Furthermore, 16.4% of our workforce 
comprises ODIs and 11.69% are women, reflecting 
our ongoing efforts in diversity and governance.
Looking Ahead: A Bright Future
Looking ahead, we remain committed to achieving 
asset-light growth through expansion in urban 
centres and underserved markets. We will continue 
to leverage digital transformation to enhance 
operational efficiency, optimise processes and 
drive profitability. Sustainability remains a core 
priority, with clear goals for all aspects. We will 
continue investing in our brands and improving the 
guest experience while ensuring long-term value 
creation for our shareholders. With these strategic 
initiatives, Lemon Tree Hotels is well-positioned to 
capture future growth opportunities and reinforce 
its leadership in the mid-market hotel sector. 
As we look to the future, our commitment goes 
beyond growth and profitability. We aspire to be the 
most inclusive and sustainable hospitality brand in 
Asia, where technology and humaneness coexist to 
deliver memorable guest experiences. Our journey 
is about building not just hotels, but communities of 
opportunity and impact.
None of this progress would have been possible 
without the relentless dedication of our people, 
the trust of our guests and the continued support 
of our shareholders and partners. I extend my 
sincere gratitude to each member of the Lemon 
Tree family who has contributed to our success in a 
rapidly evolving consumer landscape, often in the 
face of macroeconomic challenges. Your -resilience 
and commitment have enabled us to consistently 
raise the bar. With the continued trust of our 
stakeholders, we are confident of shaping a 
future where Lemon Tree Hotels leads the way in 
responsible growth.

The demand for mid- market 
hotels is growing rapidly, 
especially in Tier 2/3 cities, 
driven by rising domestic 
tourism and the increasing 
disposable income of 
the middle class. These 
segments are becoming 
increasingly attractive to 
those looking for affordable 
yet high -quality  
accommodations.
Government schemes such 
as Swadesh Darshan and 
PRASHAD have significantly 
improved infrastructure, 
opening up new regions 
for development. 
These initiatives are 
boosting connectivity 
and creating new tourism 
opportunities in previously 
underserved areas.Sustainability has become 
a high-level priority for 
both travellers and the 
hospitality industry. 
Ecofriendly practices, from 
green certifications to 
systems that are energy 
and/or water efficient, 
are now essential factors 
for both consumers 
and businesses.
Digital transformation 
unfolds in two ways. First, 
by using data to offer 
travelers personalised 
packages and boost the 
Company’s revenue. 
Second, by adopting 
digital services like mobile 
check-ins and smart 
room controls, which 
streamline and enhance the 
guest experience.The demand for wellness 
and spiritual tourism is on 
the rise as more travellers 
seek enriching experiences 
focused on health and 
spiritual growth. This trend 
is particularly strong in 
regions with rich spiritual 
heritage, such as Varanasi, 
Ayodhya and Rishikesh.
INDUSTRY TRENDS
Capitalising on India’s  
Tou r ism Boom
The Indian tourism sector is on a robust growth trajectory, fuelled by both rising domestic 
and international travel. Government initiatives such as the Swadesh Darshan and PRASHAD 
Schemes are enhancing infrastructure, further driving the development of tourism across the 
country. These advancements are creating a number of opportunities for the hospitality industry, 
especially in the mid-market segment. A growing middle class, higher disposable incomes and 
a surge in business travel are all contributing to increased demand for affordable, high-quality 
accommodations. As travellers increasingly seek value-for-money options, Lemon Tree Hotels is 
well-positioned to capitalise on this expanding market, unlocking potential for growth and market 
share expansion.
Rising Demand for Mid-market HospitalityDigital Transformation in HospitalityThe Rise of Wellness and Spiritual Tourism
Our Response
Our Company is strategically 
expanding its presence in both 
urban centres and emerging Tier 2 
and Tier 3 cities. With 212 hotels 
and 17,116 rooms, we are on track 
to reach 20,000 rooms by CY28. 
Our asset-light model ensures 
flexibility and scalability, enabling 
us to expand efficiently through 
management contracts and 
franchise agreements.Our Response
Digital transformation is reshaping 
our business in two important 
ways. First, we are gathering 
and analysing data to better 
understand our travellers, enabling 
us to design personalised packages 
while maximising overall revenue. 
Second, we are embracing digital 
services that continue to reshape 
the hospitality sector. From mobile 
check-ins to smart room controls 
and other intuitive features, we are 
simplifying and enriching the guest 
experience at every step.Our Response
Wellness tourism and spiritual 
retreats are emerging as 
strong growth drivers, and we 
are well-positioned to tap into 
this rising demand. Riding this 
wave, we are adding properties 
that offer wellness-focused 
and spiritual experiences, 
capitalising on the evolving 
preferences of both domestic and 
international travellers.
Government Initiatives Driving GrowthSustainability and Eco-conscious Travel
Our Response
With new regional airports, 
enhanced highways and tourism 
hubs coming online, we are 
capitalising on these infrastructure 
developments by expanding 
into regions that benefit from 
improved connectivity and 
emerging tourism circuits. This 
focus enables us to strengthen our 
portfolio in newly connected and 
high-potential markets.Our Response
Lemon Tree Hotels has set a clear path 
towards sustainable growth aiming for 
100% green-certified hotels by FY26. 
In FY25, we have achieved 34.15%13 of 
our hotels are already green-certified, 
with another 24% work-in-progress. 
We have targeted achievement of 50% 
renewable energy as well as a 15% 
energy intensity reduction and a 10% 
water intensity reduction by FY2614. 
This focus aligns with global trends 
and consumer demand for eco-friendly 
travel options, helping Lemon Tree 
stay competitive, as corporate clients 
include sustainability criteria in Request 
for Proposal (RFP) process while 
shortlisting hotels.

Energy Efficiency
At Lemon Tree Hotels, we have adopted a 
multi-pronged approach to improve energy 
efficiency across our properties. One of the key 
initiatives has been the installation of a Building 
Management System (BMS) at Aurika Skycity, 
Mumbai, which helps optimise energy consumption 
throughout the building. Additionally, we 
implemented an energy management system at our 
properties in Sector 60, Gurugram, which includes 
two hotels and a convention centre, enabling better 
control over energy use.
At Lemon Tree Premier and Red Fox Hotel in HITEC 
City, Hyderabad, we upgraded our fresh air units 
by retrofitting them with energy-efficient electronic 
commutator (EC) motors. These motors significantly 
reduce energy consumption while improving 
overall ventilation.
In FY25, we replaced all CFL lights with LED lights 
at our Keys properties, contributing to a substantial 
reduction in energy consumption. We also 
transitioned from Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) 
to Piped Natural Gas (PNG) at Lemon Tree Hotel, 
Indore, marking a shift to cleaner fuel and further 
enhancing our sustainability efforts.Total Energy Consumption within the Organisation in FY25 (GJ)

Renewable Energy
By the end of FY25, we successfully achieved an 
RE exit rate of 27.93%, reflecting our commitment 
to cleaner energy solutions. This transition 
has been facilitated by the installation of solar 
photovoltaic (PV) systems across our properties, 
along with open access RE agreements in hotels 
located in Delhi, Mumbai, Pune, Chennai and more 
recently, Bengaluru.
Looking ahead, we are exploring the potential for 
captive and group captive RE sites in one to two 
states, with plans for implementation once due 
diligence and financial feasibility assessments 
are completed.
The impact of our shift to renewable energy is 
twofold. First, the environmental benefits are 
significant, as RE systems have a zero emission 
factor, leading to a notable reduction in our carbon 
footprint. Second, the operating costs related to 
Heat Light Power (HLP) have decreased, as the 
cost of RE is lower than that of traditional state 
electricity board energy. We estimate that by FY26, 
when we aim to achieve 50% RE usage, we will 
save approximately ` 43 lakh in operating costs, with 
projected savings of ` 87 lakh in FY27.14%

Approach
As of FY25, we have increased the number of 
green-certified buildings to 15, with an additional 
19 hotels undergoing evaluation and audits 
by both our consultants and the Indian Green 
Building Council (IGBC). The audit results have 
led to recommendations for further sustainable 
improvements, including the application of Solar 
Reflective Index (SRI) paint on rooftops to reduce 
the building’s heat envelope, updating waste 
collection and disposal processes, and enhancing 
fresh air ventilation.
In line with our efforts to reduce the environmental 
impact of our Diesel Generator (DG) sets, we have 
implemented dual fuel systems to mitigate air 
quality concerns and ensure regulatory compliance. 
In FY25, we installed Dual Fuel Kits (DF Kits) at

Reducing our Carbon Footprint
In an effort to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) 
emissions, we are phasing out equipment with 
high levels of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and 
replacing them with more environmentally 
friendly alternatives.
The refrigeration and air conditioning systems 
are maintained under an annual contract with 
third- party Original Equipment Manufacturers 
(OEMs).Regular audits and checks by our internal 
team ensure optimal performance, reduction of energy consumption and enhancement of 
system efficiency.
Renewable energy (RE) adoption is governed by 
state-specific regulations and our RE agreements 
across India are planned and executed according 
to the criteria set by each state government. 
Over the past few years, navigating the renewable 
energy landscape has posed challenges, as some 
states have made it easier to enter RE agreements 
quickly, while others continue to experience longer

Total Water Consumption Including Bottled Water  8,81,702  3,26,791Water Stewardship
Recognising the growing scarcity of water, we are 
committed to improving the efficiency of our water 
usage across all properties. To address this, we 
have implemented several measures designed to 
reduce consumption without compromising the 
guest experience. These include lowering water 
pressure from the pipes, installing aerators on taps 
for efficient water flow and replacing older fixtures 
with water-efficient green alternatives.
We also maximise the use of flow restrictors and 
dual flush systems, further enhancing our water 
management efforts.In addition, we encourage guest participation in 
conservation through initiatives like our third- day 
linen change programme and the half-glass 
water initiative.
Water consumption across our 41 owned/leased 
hotels and 26 managed hotels increased by 
approximately 11% in FY25. This increase was 
largely driven by the full-year operation of Aurika 
Skycity, which was only operational for six months 
in FY24, and a 10% increase in occupancy. With 669 
rooms, Aurika Skycity has the largest inventory in 
India, and its water consumption grew by 32%.
Water Management
To optimise water use and ensure sustainable resource management, we have implemented 
various programmes, including recycling, wastewater treatment, rainwater harvesting and water 
conservation. Additionally, we have run water saving programmes which involve our guests and 
customers directly.

Wastewater Recycling and Reuse
In 2023, we began transitioning to purified bottled 
water to reduce plastic consumption across our 
hotels. The pilot of the Reverse Osmosis (RO) plant 
was conducted at Lemon Tree Premier and Red 
Fox Hotel in Aerocity, followed by the installation 
of a capacitive de-ionisation (CDI) system at 
Aurika Skycity in Mumbai. In 2025, we installed 
and commissioned one CDI plant for two hotels, 
Lemon Tree Premier and Red Fox Hotel in HITEC 
City, Hyderabad and four RO plants for five hotels, 
including Lemon Tree Hotel and Red Fox Hotel 
in Sector 60, Gurugram; Lemon Tree Premier, 
International Airport, Mumbai; Aurika, Udaipur; 
and Lemon Tree Premier, Ulsoor Lake, Bengaluru. 
This phased approach has resulted in a saving 
of 16,390 kgs of plastic. Additionally, we have 
observed cost savings of 5-10% at each location.
Our water management practices include a stringent 
quality control process with Standard Operating 
Procedures (SOPs) for cleaning, sanitising, filling 
and packaging the bottled water. This ensures that 
the water meets the highest safety and hygiene 
standards, reflecting our commitment to efficient 
water management and sustainability.
Despite the increase in occupancy, particularly 
at our largest hotel, Aurika Skycity, the amount 
of recycled water has remained consistent with 
FY24 levels.

Our best-in-class waste management practices focus on reducing, segregating and handling 
waste efficiently across all hotel facilities, including guest rooms, restaurants, public areas and 
operational spaces. 
To implement focused strategies, we assess waste generation across our hotels, gathering valuable 
insights that help guide our efforts. Ensuring compliance with environmental regulations set by the 
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MOEF&CC) is a primary objective for both our 
upcoming and existing hotels. To raise awareness and facilitate effective implementation of our ESG 
and Waste Management Policy, we conduct regular training sessions and provide ongoing support to 
empower our employees.
In FY25, the total waste generated at our 41 owned/leased hotels and 26 managed hotels, as covered 
in the scope of this report, was 23,33,869 kg vs. 1,368,029 kg in FY24. Hazardous waste generation 
increased to 133.17 MT, compared to 82.70 MT in FY24. Non-hazardous waste generation also saw 
an increase, rising to 2,334 MT from 1,461 MT in FY24. The increase in certain waste categories was 
primarily due to the replacement and upgrade of air conditioning systems in select hotels, alongside a 
more streamlined approach to waste data monitoring and record-keeping.

Biodiversity

effects our activities and development may have on the local ecosystem and natural resources. 
Preserving nature, biodiversity and the distinctive environments where our properties are located is 
our responsibility. As a result, we ensure that our properties do not infringe on areas designated as 
protected, such as animal reserves and national parks. We are committed to incorporating habitat 
preservation and biodiversity into all facets of our business operations, growth and acquisitions.

In FY25, across our 41 owned/leased and 26

Building Future Talent
In October 2024, we launched an Internship 
Programme under the Prime Minister’s 
Internship Scheme (PMIS), initiated by the 
Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The scheme 
offers paid internships where a part of the 
stipend is supported by us and the larger 
portion is contributed by the government. 
The objective is to nurture industry-ready 
talent for the hospitality sector and enable 
young people to access meaningful job 
opportunities with greater ease.
Further, we have entered into a memorandum 
of understanding with various Institutes of 
Hotel Management (IHM) across multiple 
cities, under the purview of the Ministry of 
Tourism. This partnership is designed to 
create greater awareness about the industry 
and its dynamics, with activities focused on 
student engagement, faculty development and 
institutional development.

Harvard Business School
Harvard Business School (HBS) conducted a 
research study jointly with Lemon Tree Hotels 
to evaluate passion and well-being among 
employees. Nearly 400 managers in Band 
5 and above (Assistant Manager and Above 
levels) participated in the study, which was 
conducted over a period of four weeks.
The research focused on how employees 
can sustain and replenish their passion over 
time, thereby reducing the risk of burnout. 
The insights and lessons shared by HBS 
are now being carefully evaluated and 
implemented in a phased manner across

Diversity and Inclusion
Our Diversity and Inclusion Policy reflects our 
commitment to building a culture of trust, 
responsibility and long-term socioeconomic 
development among our employees and within the 
communities where we operate. For nearly two 
decades, we have been a focused equal-opportunity 
employer, actively advancing diversity and inclusion 
across our workforce.
We strive to provide equitable employment 
opportunities to Opportunity Deprived Individuals 
(ODIs), including Employees with Disability (EwDs) 
and individuals from economically and socially 
marginalised backgrounds (EcoSocs). By integrating 
ODIs into our teams, we enable them to lead 
dignified lives while also fostering meaningful and 
inclusive guest experiences.
In FY25, across our 41 owned/leased and 26 
managed hotels covered in the scope of this report, 
ODIs accounted for 16.4% of our workforce. 
Gender diversity stood at 88% male and 12% 
female employees.
Key Diversity and Inclusion Initiatives
Over the last 18 years, building a culture of inclusion 
and diversity has become a part of the DNA of our 
Company. We have embedded it across multiple 
departments within a hotel and across multiple 
hotels in the city and then across multiple cities. We have also done trials and internships across 
multiple disability types including Down Syndrome, 
Intellectual and Developmental Disability and 
Autism. The exploration of different departments 
and bringing in new disability types requires a 
structured process of observations, followed by 
job mapping and then planning the training for 
interns with special needs. It is this flow that allows 
us to build our base and higher more Employees 
with Disability.

Talent Management   
In August 2024, we introduced the Hotel General 
Managers (HGMs) Development Programme as a 
structured three-month initiative to strengthen 
functional learning and leadership effectiveness. 
The programme is designed to help HGMs better 
understand their roles, recognise individual skills 
and knowledge and align their hotel leadership 
teams with Lemon Tree’s evolving strategy and 
vision. Learning is delivered through online sessions 
conducted by Corporate Function Heads, as well 
as self-reading, videos, simulations, live cases and 
case studies.
In FY25, driven by our rapid growth plans, we 
opened 12 new hotels in India and overseas. 
This expansion created multiple internal job 
opportunities for our high-potential employees, 
enabling them to take on higher responsibilities and 
move into roles such as Deputy Head of Department 
or Head of Department at the new properties. 
Beyond being a strong career advancement 
strategy, this approach allows us to organically 
embed Lemon Tree’s culture into new hotels as 
they open.

Health, Safety and Well-being
Health and safety are top priorities for us and 
our Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) 
Management System covers all employees and 
hotels. We routinely identify potential work-related 
hazards, conduct both routine and non-routine risk 
assessments and are committed to ensuring that 
no occupational health risks affect our employees, 
contractors, guests, communities or the public. 
We aim to achieve zero incidents across all 
our operations.
Fire Safety
All hotels are equipped with automatic smoke 
detectors, audible alarms, fire extinguishers, 
hydrants, portable firefighting equipment and 
emergency lighting to ensure preparedness.
Food Safety
A comprehensive Food Production Manual 
guides training and procedures across 
receiving, handling, storing, cooking, 
reheating and serving food, ensuring that 
all food and beverages meet the highest 
safety standards.Security
We employ trained security personnel, 
install monitoring and search equipment and 
maintain standardised response procedures to 
safeguard employees, guests and visitors.
Community Well-being
By hiring locally and sourcing from 
nearby suppliers, we contribute to local 
economic development and support 
community resilience.Equipment Safety
Designated trained operators oversee 
equipment handling, supported by detailed 
safety procedures and maintenance protocols 
followed by authorised personnel.
Promotion of Employee Health
We support employee well-being through 
health camps, smoking cessation initiatives, 
dietary counselling, mental health workshops 
and fitness programmes.Sanitization
Regular cleaning and sanitization of high-touch 
surfaces such as doorknobs, countertops, 
room keys and EDC machines ensure a 
hygienic environment for all.
Risk Management
Health and safety risks are regularly 
reviewed and managed through design and 
engineering controls, preventive maintenance, 
administrative measures and structured 
safety training.Focus Areas

Hazard Identification and Mitigation
We have implemented an Incident Tracking System 
that enables us to detect potential hazards early 
and take proactive measures to mitigate risks. 
Reported hazards are acted upon immediately, with 
preventive steps put in place to avoid recurrence.
Employee safety remains central to our approach, 
supported by comprehensive safety training 
programmes and well-documented emergency 
response plans. In addition, regular safety audits 
and risk assessments actively involve employees 
in identifying areas for improvement, ensuring 
hazards are promptly addressed and the risk of 
incidents minimised.
Health and Safety Governance 
Our Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) 
standards, rules and procedures are overseen 
at the corporate level by our OHS Committee. 
Each hotel also has a local OHS Committee to 
ensure compliance with regional regulations. 
These committees focus on incident analysis and 
prioritising mitigation actions. In addition, all our 
hotels maintain trained first-aid personnel on site 
to provide immediate support in case of medical 
emergencies, thereby safeguarding the well-being 
of employees, guests and visitors.
In FY25, 51.29% of our full-time employees across 
the 41 owned/leased and 26 managed hotels 
within the scope of this report received training 
on health and safety measures, including 47.99% 
male employees and 76.26% female employees. 
This compares with FY24, when 40% of employees 
were trained, including 39% male and 48% 
female employees.Zero

Working conditionsHuman Rights
We have implemented a Human Rights Policy that 
sets out clear expectations for employees, business 
partners and third-party contractors. This policy 
is aligned with international standards such as the 
Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) 
and the International Labour Organisation (ILO) 
Declaration, reinforcing our commitment to uphold 
human rights as a core value across our operations.
We actively raise awareness to prevent human 
rights abuse and promote community well-being. 
Our zero-tolerance approach addresses issues 
such as sexual harassment, discrimination, child 
labour and all forms of forced labour or exploitation. 
We also monitor construction sites to prevent 
violations, misconduct, unfair treatment and workplace harassment, including for employees 
affiliated with associations and unions. Reported 
violations are thoroughly investigated by our 
Vigilance Officer to ensure safety and fairness 
for all.
In FY25, our workforce across the 41 owned/
leased and 26 managed hotels within the scope of 
this report comprised 5,621 full-time employees. 
Of these, 108 employees (95 male and 13 female) 
across the owned/leased hotels were members 
of trade unions. None of the employees in the 
26 managed hotels were part of trade unions or 
covered by collective bargaining agreements. 
Overall, 1.92% of our full-time employees 
are covered under trade unions/collective 
bargaining agreements.

Delivering Customer Satisfaction
We place strong emphasis on online reputation 
management (ORM) and follow a structured process 
involving our hotel operations and ORM teams to 
promptly address any service issues or deficiencies. 
For us, customer satisfaction is a core priority.
In FY25, our customer base continued to expand 
across the 41 owned/leased and 26 managed 
hotels within the scope of this report, with a total 
of 14,10,860 customers compared to 13,72,871 
in FY24.
Building on insights from ORM data, in FY25, 
we introduced a number of targeted service 
improvement initiatives. These included product 
upgrades and renovations across the group, 
along with re-training programmes for our 
front-end staff to further improve and consolidate 
service standards.
Customer Feedback Management
We continuously enhance our services and ensure 
customer satisfaction by valuing guest feedback and 
responding with care. Feedback is central to our 
business philosophy and we encourage guests to 
share their experiences through multiple channels, 
including our Guest Satisfaction Tracking System 
(GSTS), online platforms such as TripAdvisor and 
social media, as well as online travel agencies 
(OTAs) like Booking.com  and MakeMyTrip.
At Lemon Tree Hotels, we act promptly on guest 
feedback as part of our commitment to excellence. 
Our Learning and Development (L&D) team reviews 
each negative or passive comment across GSTS 
and online platforms using Root Cause Analysis, focusing on both people and process-related factors 
to identify underlying issues. Recurring themes are 
addressed by refining brand standards to ensure 
consistently high-quality experiences.
To resolve concerns quickly, the L&D team 
provides re-briefings and targeted corrective 
training where required, working closely with hotel 
operations teams. The voice of our customers 
guides our journey, helping us to strengthen 
service quality, build genuine connections and drive 
continuous growth.
Promoting Sustainability through 
Guest Participation
We actively build awareness around sustainability 
with our guests and prioritise involving them in our 
initiatives. Through our communication channels, 
we share information on our waste management 
practices and their positive environmental impact.
Our guest engagement programme includes water 
recycling posters in washrooms and our third-day 
linen change initiative, which encourages guests to 
conserve water by opting not to change their linen 
daily. This empowers travellers to play a meaningful 
role in preserving this critical resource during 
their stay.
At our restaurants, the half-glass water initiative has 
been well received by guests, who often recognise 
and appreciate these efforts through feedback and 
social media posts.
Loyalty and Rewards Programme
In FY25, we launched Infinity Rewards, our new 
loyalty programme designed to strengthen guest 
retention, drive direct bookings and reward repeat 
customers. Members earn and redeem reward coins 
whenever they stay at Lemon Tree, making each 
visit more rewarding and memorable.
The programme features four membership tiers 
— Silver, Gold, Platinum and Platinum Plus, each 
offering exclusive benefits. These include discounts 
on room rates, best price guarantee, free in-room 
Wi-Fi and, for Platinum and Platinum Plus members, 
complimentary buffet breakfast. Guests earn reward 
coins on every rupee spent across room stays, food 
and beverages and other services. Redemption is 
simple and seamless, with free stays bookable 
online at participating Lemon Tree properties.
Since its launch, Infinity Rewards has seen rapid 
adoption. By the end of March 2025, the programme 
had grown to 19,95,806 members, reflecting strong 
guest interest and loyalty to the brand.Guest Stays

Responsible Supply Chain Practices
We follow a Supplier Code of Conduct that reflects our commitment to a sustainable and ethical 
supply chain. It requires all vendors, suppliers and service providers to adopt responsible practices 
and comply with international standards, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) 
and International Labour Organisation (ILO) conventions. The Code covers minimum wages, human 
rights, health and safety, environmental compliance, labour practices, freedom of association, ethical 
conduct and transparent business operations.

Our Code of Conduct
Our Code of Conduct (CoC) applies to all members 
of the Board, leadership team, senior management, 
and employees. It embodies the Company’s 
commitment to fairness, transparency, and 
professionalism, guiding individuals to perform 
their duties with integrity and uphold the highest 
ethical standards.By fostering ethical and transparent practices, our 
CoC ensures accountable management aligned with 
the Company’s vision and values. All related-party 
transactions, including those involving interested 
Directors or potential conflicts of interest, are 
reviewed and approved by the Audit Committee 
and the Board, with material transactions requiring 
specific Board approval.

We aim to deliver long-term value to all 
stakeholders, shareholders, employees, guests, 
business partners and society at large, through a 
governance system that enhances transparency and 
efficiency across corporate processes.Board Performance Evaluation 
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee 
(NRC) undertakes an annual formal evaluation 
of the performance of the Board of Directors, its 
Committees and individual Directors in line with 
the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the 
applicable SEBI (LODR) Regulations. The evaluation 
is conducted in a systematic and structured manner, 
beginning with the collection of inputs from all 
Directors and followed by an assessment against 
pre-defined qualitative and quantitative parameters.
The parameters cover, inter alia, the effectiveness 
of the Board’s role in strategy formulation, 
performance monitoring, risk oversight, corporate 
governance, compliance with statutory and 
regulatory requirements, organisational culture and 
talent management.
In compliance with statutory requirements, the 
Independent Directors carry out a separate 
evaluation of the performance of Non-Independent 
Directors, including the Chairperson, as well as the 
functioning of the Board as a collective body.
The evaluation is undertaken in accordance with 
a framework and criteria approved by the Board, 
ensuring transparency, objectivity, and a balanced 
appraisal of the performance of individual Directors, 
the Committees and the Board as a whole.

Grievance Redressal
Our Company has a robust grievance redressal 
framework to ensure transparency, accountability, 
and timely resolution of concerns raised by 
employees, shareholders and other stakeholders. 
This framework is overseen by the Audit Committee, 
with the Chairperson directly addressing exceptional 
matters. During the reporting period, no grievances 
were recorded.
The framework is supported by our Company’s 
Whistle Blower Policy (Vigil Mechanism), 
established in compliance with the Companies 
Act, 2013 and SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. 
The Policy provides secure channels for reporting 
unethical behaviour, fraud, financial irregularities 
or violations of the Code of Conduct. It ensures 
confidentiality, protection against victimisation, 
and permits anonymous reporting through sealed 
letters or email to the Vigilance Officer ( svp_hr@
lemontreehotels.com ) or the Chairperson of the 
Audit Committee ( praveengargias@gmail.com ), with 
direct access to the Audit Committee Chairperson 
in exceptional cases. Disclosures are investigated 
objectively and resolved in a time-bound manner, 
with records retained for at least five years.
General grievances are typically resolved within 
24-72 hours through a structured escalation 
process, with an additional channel available via 
OurVoice@lemontreehotels.com . Awareness is 
reinforced through the General Service Rules & 
Regulations and New Hire Orientation, while data 
from the Employee Satisfaction Tracking System 
is reviewed to identify recurring issues and drive 
continuous improvement. Our Company also 
addresses all shareholder-related complaints, 
including those concerning share transfers, 
allotments, refunds, certificates, financial 
statements and annual reports.Data Privacy and Security
Our Company prioritises data security and 
governance through a robust framework that 
incorporates well-defined cybersecurity measures to 
safeguard the personal information of stakeholders. 
Security protocols are reviewed and updated 
regularly to reflect technological advancements 
and evolving regulatory requirements, ensuring 
protection against data loss, misuse, wrongful 
disclosure, alteration or destruction.
In line with the Data Privacy Policy, our Company 
provides clear information on the personal 
data collected, its purpose, and how it is used, 
processed, shared and transferred. Personal data 
is retained only for the necessary duration, in 
compliance with legal, regulatory, contractual or 
statutory obligations, and is securely deleted or 
archived once the retention period expires.
To strengthen oversight, our Company engages 
internal auditors and, where necessary, external 
auditors to conduct IT control audits every six 
months, with any anomalies reported to the Board 
for review.
During the reporting period, our Company 
experienced no data breaches.Building Sustainability Awareness
We aim to strengthen our work culture by advancing sustainability through targeted training and awareness 
programmes for the Board of Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and employees. These sessions cover ESG 
principles, business strategy, safety protocols, digital transformation and risk management.

Internal Audit Methodology
Alignment with Corporate HoDs
• Individual meeting with Corporate HoDs are held before 
initiation of audit cycle.
• Objective of meetings is to evaluate existing audit 
parameters, key focus areas, communication of changes in 
existing SOPs/guidelines etc.• Rating allocation on various audit parameters.
• Audit execution is defined and agreed before initiating the 
audit process.
• Action plans agreed with respective HoD are shared 
through MoMs with stakeholders including Corporate HoDs.
• Summary of key issues are presented to Audit Committee.
Audit Execution and Field Closure
• Respective unit Cluster Head and GMs are intimated before 
initiation of the audit.
• No intimation is given to Units under surprise audits.
• Sharing of audit queries with process owners.
• Exceptions are also reported to process owners and unit GM for discussion.
• Closure meeting is done with Unit GM and respective HoDs 
at the end of each audit.
• Post discussion observations and audit ratings are agreed 
and signed off by GM.
Issues Compilation and Presentation to Stakeholders
• Post closure of all audits, audit issues observed in units are 
compiled at the Corporate with ratings.
• Department wise issues are shared with Corporate HoDs 
for their reference and comments.
• Review meeting with Corporate HoDs is scheduled for 
discussion on issues.• The discussion focuses on root cause analysis and 
corresponding action plans.
• Action plans agreed with respective HoD are shared 
through MoMs with stakeholders including Corporate HoDs.
• Summary of key issues are presented to 
Audit Committee.

Macroeconomic 
Environment and 
Government Policy Impact
India's economic environment continues to provide a 
robust foundation for the hospitality sector's growth 
trajectory. The country has demonstrated strong 
economic resilience, with GDP registering a nominal 
growth of 9.9% and real growth of 6.5% in FY25, 
positioning India as the world's fastest-growing major 
economy with projected growth of 6.3-6.8% in FY26. 
(Source:  )
The services sector, which includes hospitality, has 
strengthened its position as a key growth driver, 
expanding its contribution to Gross Value Added (GVA) 
from 50.6% in FY14to 55% in FY25 while employing 
approximately 30% of the workforce. This expansion 
directly benefits our operations as it indicates sustained 
domestic consumption and demand for hotel rooms, 
especially for business travel. (Source:  )
Government Policy Support and 
Investment Climate
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows surged by 27% 
to ₹3.40 lakh Crores ($40.67 billion) in April-December 
2024, with cumulative FDI reaching ₹89.85 lakh Crores 
($1.05 trillion) since April 2000. The government's 
target of achieving $100 billion annual FDI inflows 
creates a favourable investment climate that supports 
the expansion of the hospitality sector through 
increased business travel and corporate demand.  
(Source:  )
The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes with 
an outlay of ₹1.97 lakh Crores, across 14 sectors, are 
driving industrial growth and creating new business 
centres, directly benefitting our hotel locations in 
emerging industrial hubs. Additionally, inflation control 
measures have successfully reduced retail inflation 
to 4.6% in FY25, the lowest since FY19, enhancing 
consumer spending power and travel propensity. 
(Source:  )
Digital Transformation and Payment 
Infrastructure Impact
India's digital payment revolution significantly impacts 
our operations, delivery of service and the overall 
guest experience. The country now accounts for 
49% of global real-time digital transactions, with 
UPI processing unprecedented volumes. This digital 
infrastructure advancement enables seamless guest 
experiences and operational efficiency improvements 
across our properties. (Source:  )Management

and Analysis

Operational Benefits of Digital Infrastructure
• Enhanced guest check-in/check-out processes 
through digital payment integration
• Improved revenue collection efficiency with 
reduced payment processing costs
• Better analytical capabilities to use guest data 
for personalised service delivery
• Streamlined vendor payments and supply 
chain management
The government's push for digital transactions, 
evidenced by IMPS processing 441 million transactions 
worth ₹6.01 lakh Crores in December 2024, creates 
opportunities for operational cost optimisation and 
enhanced guest satisfaction through technology-
enabled services. (Source:  )
The hospitality sector in India recorded a nationwide 
occupancy of 63-65% in CY24, with an Average Room 
Rate (ARR) of ₹7,800–8,000 and RevPAR between ₹5,000–5,200, registering a 10-12% YoY growth. 
These figures represent a solid performance, though 
still marginally below pre-pandemic highs. (Source: 
 )
India’s total air traffic in 2024 reached 400.8 
million, with 325.3 million domestic and 75.5 million 
international travellers, marking continued recovery 
and surpassing 2019 levels. Foreign Tourist Arrivals 
(FTAs) grew to 9.65 million, with an expectation 
to exceed pre-COVID numbers in FY26. (Source: 
 )
The government’s sustained investment in 
infrastructure, including new airports, highways and 
rail corridors—and promotion of spiritual circuits like 
Ayodhya, Varanasi, Kedarnath and Tirupati is expected 
to further propel tourism. The 'Wed in India' campaign 
and initiatives in medical, cruise and rural tourism are 
further driving leisure and business segments.

This supply expansion pattern validates our strategic focus on emerging markets while maintaining presence in 
established commercial centres. (Source:  )Barriers to Entry
The Indian hospitality sector presents formidable 
barriers to entry that protect established players while 
creating significant challenges for new entrants to the 
market. These structural impediments have contributed 
to the sector's consolidation and the sustained 
competitive advantage of experienced operators like 
Lemon Tree Hotels.
1.  Land Acquisition and Development 
Constraints
 Prime Location Scarcity in Tier 1 Cities
  The most significant barrier to entry in the 
Indian hospitality sector remains the scarcity 
and escalating cost of prime real estate in 
metropolitan markets. Tier 1 cities such as 
Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai 
have witnessed land prices appreciation of 12-
15% annually over the past decade, making hotel 
development economically challenging for new 
entrants. Prime commercial land in these markets 
now commands prices ranging from ₹50,000 to 
₹2,00,000 per square foot, substantially increasing 
project costs and extending payback periods.
  The shortage of appropriately zoned land for 
hospitality development compounds this challenge. 
Municipal authorities maintain strict zoning 
regulations and the conversion of agricultural or 
residential land for commercial hospitality use 
involves lengthy approval processes spanning 
18-36 months. Additionally, the requirement for 
substantial parking facilities, fire safety compliance 
and environmental clearances further constrains 
available development options.
  Regulatory Complexity and Approval 
Processes
  The hospitality sector operates under a complex 
web of regulatory requirements spanning multiple 
government levels and departments. New entrants 
must navigate over 50 different approvals and 
clearances, including:
• State-level licenses:  Excise permits, 
trade licenses, building approvals, fire 
safety clearances
• Municipal clearances:  Water and 
sewerage connections, solid waste 
management permissions, health 
trade permits
• Central regulations:  Pollution Control 
Board clearances, Forest Department 
approvals (for hill stations), Archaeological 
Survey clearances (for heritage locations)• Industry-specific requirements: 
Tourism Department approvals, star 
classification procedures, foreign 
exchange permissions
  This regulatory maze typically requires 12-18 
months for completion and involves significant 
compliance costs, often deterring potential new 
entrants who lack the resources and expertise to 
navigate these complexities effectively.
2. Capital Intensity and Financial Barriers
  High Capital Requirements and Scale 
Economics
  Hotel development in India requires substantial 
initial capital investment, typically ranging from 
₹80-150 Lakhs per room for mid-scale properties 
to ₹3-5 Crores per room for luxury establishments. 
These capital requirements, coupled with 
construction periods of 24-36 months, create 
significant financial barriers for new entrants.
  Return on Investment (RoI) without achieving 
economies of scale remains challenging, as hotels 
require minimum occupancy levels of 65-70% to 
achieve operational breakeven. New properties 
typically experience 12-18 months of ramp-up 
period to achieve stabilised operations, during which 
they incur substantial losses while building market 
awareness and establishing distribution channels.
  Due to the hospitality sector's asset-heavy 
nature, achieving competitive unit economics 
requires portfolio scale for effective procurement, 
marketing, and operational efficiency. Single-
property operators struggle to compete with 
established chains that benefit from centralised 
services, bulk purchasing power, and shared 
marketing costs.
  Market Saturation and Brand Loyalty 
Challenges
  Established hospitality brands have developed 
strong customer loyalty through decades 
of consistent service delivery and extensive 
distribution networks. Corporate clients, who 
constitute 60-70% of business hotel revenue, 
typically prefer working with recognised brands 
that offer standardised quality, extensive 
geographical coverage, and sophisticated booking 
and billing systems. 
  The Indian hospitality market has witnessed 
consolidation among the top 10 players, who 
now control approximately 45% of organised 
supply. These established operators benefit from 
economies of scale in marketing, technology 
systems and talent acquisition, thereby creating 
competitive advantages that are difficult for new 
entrants to replicate.
